newsitem.title: CHINA: Small HK banks stretch valuations with recent rise.
newsitem.headline: Small HK banks stretch valuations with recent rise.

text.p: Some of Hong Kong's small banks have enjoyed a strong rally in the Hong Kong stock market this week, led by Ka Wah Bank Ltd, but while analysts see strong growth for the sector, they say valuations are stretched.
"We are pretty neutral on the sector now. We are expecting to see some consolidation," said Shannon Garrett, investment analyst at SocGen-Crosby Securities.
"We are long-term buyers on Wing Hang, Dah Sing and Liu Chong Hing. The rest look as though the speculative rally has pushed valuations beyond current fundamentals," she said.
While blue chips have been under pressure, ending the week with a loss of 400.83 points, or 2.43 percent, at 16,096.88 on Friday, some small banks have moved ahead.
Ka Wah Bank gained 68 percent this week, closing at HK$14.15 on Friday. The company is considering becoming a wholly-owned subsidiary of a holding company to be incorporated in Bermuda.
Analysts said investors were speculating that Ka Wah parent China International Trust and Investment Corp (CITIC) would inject assets into the holding company.
"It is expected to become a financial-related conglomerate," said Peregrine Securities head of research Keith Wu.

Other banks have also been swept up in frenzy for red chips, linked to hopes that Chinese parents may inject assets into their Hong Kong units. But Merrill Lynch analyst Keith Irving said he was not convinced this would apply to small banks.

"We do not subscribe to the asset injection story so strongly in the small banks. The value has to come back to what they can deliver and the rapid rise implies an important pick-up in earnings growth and we just do not see that happening."
Irving said he expected most small banks to produce "relatively healthy" earnings growth but preferred the banks which were diversifying into retail financial services, like Wing Hang Bank Ltd.

"It is the most efficient small bank in the sector," he said, forecasting a compound annual growth rate of 20 percent for the company. "If you combine the growth rate with the P.E. (price earnings) valuation, it is the least expensive," he said.
Garrett forecast annual earnings growth of 20 percent for both Wing Hang Bank and Dah Sing Financial Holdings Ltd through to 1999, buoyed by their expanding consumer credit businesses.
"They are expanding into higher margin lending," she said.
Liu Chong Hing Bank Ltd should benefit from its links to COSCO Pacific Ltd, Garrett added, predicting 18 percent annual growth on a three-year basis.
COSCO Pacific, an arm of state-owned China Overseas Shipping Corp, has agreed to buy 20 percent of Liu Chong Hing Bank.
Analysts noted that smaller banks had produced better than expected earnings so far this year.

"If you look at their results, they have outperformed all the big banks in the first half," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at BNP PrimeEast Securities. "The PE ratings of most of them are below the bigger banks in Hong Kong," he said.
Wing Hang reported a 27 percent rise in net profit for the six months to June 30 and Dah Sing posted a 39.7 percent surge.
But Alan Hutcheson, a banking analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said it would be difficult for small banks to maintain those growth rates going forward.
"All the interims we have seen from the small banks were pretty much as, or better than expected. It is a question of looking forward to what kind of growth rates they can maintain.
"I don't think they can maintain the same growth rates as in the first half," he said.
